problem_context.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
problem_context.statement: An array nums was sorted in strictly increasing order and then rotated at an unknown position. Given nums and target, return the target index or -1 if target is absent.

items: nums contains distinct values and is a rotation of a strictly increasing array.

python.display_signature: def search(self, nums: list[int], target: int) -> int

expected_approaches.summary: At each midpoint identify the sorted half, then keep it only if its value range can contain target.
expected_approaches.applicability: Distinct values in a rotated strictly increasing array.
assumptions: Distinct endpoints make one sorted half distinguishable.
key_invariants: If target exists, it remains inside the retained interval.
At least one current half is normally ordered.
tradeoffs: Boundary comparisons must be inclusive in the right places.
common_failure_modes: discarding the sorted half containing target

alternative_approaches.summary: Locate the rotation pivot and binary-search the relevant sorted segment.
alternative_approaches.applicability: When separating pivot logic improves clarity.
assumptions: The same distinct-value rotation assumptions hold.
key_invariants: The pivot partitions two sorted ranges.

reference_solutions.source_code: class Solution { public: int search(vector<int> nums,int target){int left=0,right=nums.size()-1;while(left<=right){int mid=left+(right-left)/2;if(nums[mid]==target)return mid;if(nums[left]<=nums[mid]){if(nums[left]<=target&&target<nums[mid])right=mid-1;else left=mid+1;}else{if(nums[mid]<target&&target<=nums[right])left=mid+1;else right=mid-1;}}return -1;} };

class Solution { public int search(int[] nums,int target){int left=0,right=nums.length-1;while(left<=right){int mid=left+(right-left)/2;if(nums[mid]==target)return mid;if(nums[left]<=nums[mid]){if(nums[left]<=target&&target<nums[mid])right=mid-1;else left=mid+1;}else if(nums[mid]<target&&target<=nums[right])left=mid+1;else right=mid-1;}return -1;} }

complexity_expectations.diagnostic_goal: One half is removed each iteration under distinct-value assumptions.

common_misconceptions.diagnostic_goal: A globally rotated order cannot use ordinary midpoint direction logic.

failure_modes.diagnostic_goal: Include endpoints when deciding whether target lies in a sorted half.

counterexamples.purpose: The target sits on a sorted-half boundary.

constraint_mutations.diagnostic_goal: Equal boundary values can make the sorted-half decision ambiguous; discarding duplicates one at a time can degrade worst-case time to O(n), so the base O(log n) guarantee no longer holds.

probe_opportunities.diagnostic_goal: Defend how a sorted half and target range justify discarding the other half.
